spans.text: The building isn't as bright and spacious as I thought. Quite the contrary, it's pitch dark. Not a ray of sunlight penetrates into the construction; I can't even orient myself.
If it weren't for the solid surface beneath my feet, I wouldn't even be sure I'm actually standing on the ground.
Kalina, could you scan this area?
It seems to be a subspace in the database. Access authorizations seem to be a bit jumbled and some pre-established subroutines have been written into the program...
Uh... In a language I can understand please?
That is to say, it's like walking into an opera. Everything is written and pre-arranged.
Opera, huh...
Henrietta?
Are you still here?
As if to answer my call, her soft, delicate hand squeezes mine with more force, and she keeps leading me in the same direction.
Even though I still can't see a thing, I feel somewhat more reassured having her with me.
Are there no lights in the building?
No.
"Darkness is the best place for imagination because everything in here is unknown."
That's what Signore Marco once said.
Marco?
That's Angelica's Handler.
Are you sure you're feeling alright, Signore Giuseppe? You seem to be rather forgetful today.
Oh, sorry, but I'm fine. I'm just a bit slow.
So even you have your careless moments. Are you scared because it's so dark in here?
Then let me sing a song for you.
Joy, bright spark of divinity, Daughter of Elysium..."
"Fire-inspired we tread thy sanctuary..."
Do you like Symphony No. 9 a lot?
We sang it together the night we watched the meteor shower.
No matter what plight I may face, whenever I sing that song, I think back to that moment and feel calm again.
That's a pretty good way to comfort yourself.
Henrietta's chuckle drifts back toward me; she seems very happy.
After a while, she comes to a halt.
We're here. Angelica's Vita is the closest so it's pretty easy to locate.
But I'm not seeing anything?
There's a door over here. Can't you see it?
Henrietta's arm extends into the dark, and light starts seeping through as if there really was a door there.
Let's go in, Signore Giuseppe.
I walk into a scene of dazzling brightness and busy hubbub.
Having emerged from a dark and quiet place, I have to stop and squint to let my eyes adjust to the new environment.
Signore Marco! If you don't hurry, I'm going to leave you behind!
Marco?
Isn't that Angelica's Handler?
There you are, Cano...
What are you talking about, Signore Marco?! I've always been here.
Is your head addled with sleep?
I take in my surroundings. Cano and I are standing in a street.
There are no reflective glasses or digital displays, just the solid austerity that's characteristic of architecture in the olden days. Other than the sun, nothing here pierces the eye.
From what I learned in school, this seems to be pre-WWIII Rome.
However, I've lost track of Henrietta. I look around anxiously but can't find her anywhere.
Henrietta?
I'm here, Signore Giuseppe. I'm standing right next to you, but I can't seem to touch you or anything here – how strange.
Can you not see me?
This is the first time I've entered someone else's Vita. I wonder if this is supposed to happen...
Of course! Because of the pre-established subroutine, anyone not in the script is excluded from the scene.
Then how come I can talk to Cano?
Your login ID has been automatically changed to the Handler named Marco. Maybe this has something to do with the subroutine as well?
You mean I'll have to pretend to be another person in here?
Well... Do your best!
I'm sorry... I volunteered to bring you into Vita, but now I'm completely useless...
Don't worry, just stay by my side. It would be great if you could answer whatever questions I have.
Umm... Sure! I'll tell you whatever you want to know! You just have to ask, Signore Giuseppe!
Right then... It's time to start playing this Marco.
...Signore Marco? Why have you gone all quiet?
I was just joking. You're not mad at me, are you?
Oh... No, I'm not.
I'm just glad that you're okay.
Hmm? Of course I'm okay. You're so weird today, Signore Marco.
Oh, no! We'll miss the train back if we don't hurry!
If we get home late, you'll get another lecture from Jean!
What if he gets angry and sends you off to Hereford?!
Cano drags me on by the hem of my coat in great hurry. I try to gather my thoughts as I run after her.
Cano doesn't seem to have recognized me as the Commander. Rather, she's treating me as a Handler who exists in this world.
Has her memory been altered? Is that why none of the Dolls have returned?
I've got to get to the bottom of this...
I've completed my training today!
I saw the data. You did great.
Heheh, Cano is the best Cyborg!
Signore Marco, will I get a reward for doing well today?
Reward?
Huh? You haven't forgotten, have you?
You promised you'd buy me the sequel to the picture book if I perform well!
The picture book?
You know, "The Prince of the Kingdom of Pasta"!
The speed at which time passes can be manually adjusted with this account. Three days have elapsed since I entered this story.
I have temporarily paused the story, causing Cano to freeze in a rather comical posture.
I open up the document. Apparently, the picture book was written by this Marco for his Cyborg.
However, at this point in time, it shouldn't be in public circulation.
Have you ever heard of the picture book, Henrietta?
Of course; the story is quite famous within the Agency.
But you can't buy the book in any bookstore, right? After all, Marco wrote it with his colleagues.
Hmm... That is correct, but anything is possible in Vita.
Is that so...? Must be the subroutine again.
I resume the story. Cano is looking expectantly at me with sparkling eyes.
Oh, you're right.
Now I remember. Since you did so well today, I've got to reward you.
Then are we...
Yep, we're getting that book today.
Hooray! Thank youuuuuu, Signore Marco!
Cano runs out of the office cheering.
I've been reading and re-reading this story, hoping to find something while I skip through moments, but I remain disappointed.
Cano's memories show no sign of returning, and I haven't caught even a glimpse of Angelica, the original owner of this Vita.

Angelica isn't on the list of Cyborgs who work under the Agency. All records of her have been replaced by Cano. Still, despite the lack of result from my investigation, I did find a lot more information about the Agency and their Cyborgs.

Cyborgs can't hope to compare with T-Dolls when it comes to combat capabilities. Through augmentation, they can only make the girls about as strong as the average adult man, though I suppose that's enough for a special service organization who needs to keep a low profile...

However, it's still very inhumane. They drastically reduce the girls' lifespan and even brainwash them. They take everything away from them but give them a first-class living environment as if out of magnanimity. What on earth are they thinking at this Agency?
Commander, can you hear me?
Anything new?
I've been studying the subroutines in there. It seems that only the corresponding authorized user can alter the program.
You can't do it from outside?
My access keeps being denied. I think in order to solve the problem, you must first find this girl called Angelica.
A story is unfolding by the script in there. If you let it run its course, the subroutine will eventually lose effect.
So I have to let the whole thing play out and guide it to the scripted ending...?
That seems to be the case.
I don't know why Cano has replaced Angelica in this story, but as long as she's still in there as a character of the play, you're bound to run into her at some point.
How can you be so sure?
Because it's a story. As the original main character, she's got to make an appearance sooner or later. That's the rule that all stories must abide by.
That explanation sounds way too meta... Anyway, I'll give it a try.
Ah... I don't know why but somehow it feels like it's been ages since I last had an outing!
Everything looks new to me.
That's probably because you've been busy with missions.
Missions from the Agency are the most important, aren't they?
But after work, it's only right to march~ ahead~ happily like this!
You're really cheerful.
My, you've bought a lot of books. I thought there was only one new picture book?
We don't get to go out often, so Claes and the others have asked me to get them some books too.
I don't have to pay out of my own pocket anyway, so I agreed to help, hehehe~
Sheesh.
Still, do you really need to read while you walk? Why don't you read it after we get home?
But I'm DYING to find out what happens next!
Cano explains as she twirls merrily in the street, waving her picture book around and being completely oblivious to everything else.
Meanwhile, around the corner of the street, a girl is being dragged along by the leash of a gigantic dog.
Hahaha, slow down, Perro!
The girl is wearing a pretty dress and leather shoes, her heels pitter-pattering crisply against the ground.
The sun shines mildly on her hair and clothes, casting a warm halo around her entire figure.
Whoa!
Woof woof woof!
Cano and the girl collide into each other as the dog barks.
Ow, ow, ow... S-Sorry about that! Are you okay?
Cano jumps back on her feet and hurries over to help the other girl up.
I'm alright, don't worry.
The girl with long, brown hair smiles kindly even though she just got knocked over. She looks exactly like a well-mannered little lady from a rich family.
She dusts herself off lightly and answers Cano with a smile while trying to soothe her spooked dog.
Oh...
What is it, Henrietta?
That's Angelica. Why would she be here?
I've kind of figured out who this girl is based on intuition, though her sudden appearance still takes me by surprise.
The main character is bound to make an appearance...I suppose...?
What exactly is the point of taking Angelica out of her own role in the play?
I'm really sorry!
It's okay, really! Even Perro thinks it's no big deal, don't you, Perro?
Woof!
In that case, we'll be leaving~
Oh, one second. May I ask what book it is that you're holding...?
Huh? This?
It's the very popular "Prince of the Kingdom of Pasta"! Have you never read it?
No...I haven't, but...
Angelica takes the picture book from Cano.
But...somehow it feels very familiar...
That's the picture book Signore Marco wrote for her, how come she doesn't remember it at all?
We all know it's not her fault, nor is it Signore Marco's fault...
So whose fault is it?
At that moment, an ear-splitting screech of a car's tires draws dangerously close. I haven't encountered any enemy here so far, but I can tell our interceptors are far from friendly.
Cano also looks nervous. Clattering footsteps come from all around us – we're about to be surrounded.
Cano, get Angelica out of—
Before I can even finish, a burst of bullets are fired in my direction!
A force jerks me back abruptly from behind and I land heavily on the ground.
A bullet whizzes past the top of my head and hits the wall behind me, producing a deafening crack.
Meanwhile, Cano has already drawn her weapon and started returning fire.
Are you okay?! It's a terrorist attack by the Five Republics!
I'm fine! Get them all!
I turn around and see Angelica staring at me with a terrified look on her face. It was undoubtedly her that just saved me by dragging me off my feet.
No ordinary human with normal reflexes could've done that, but right now she looks exactly like an ordinary girl who's very frightened.
Thanks for that.
I... What...
Sitting on the ground, Angelica stares dubiously at her hands, then at me.
Signore...Marco?
You know my name?
I shouldn't know you...but why do I feel like...
Angelica's eyes gradually grow more resolved. I can sense the airs of a "rich girl" dissipating from her.
We can't let them get any closer. Please give me a gun, Signore Marco.
But you...
I can fight! A gun, Signore Marco!
I gape for a second, then I hand my sidearm to Angelica.
Once she takes it, she immediately heads over to Cano and covers the flank almost instinctively.

That's right, protecting our Handler is our most sacred duty, one that we can never forget. I was a little unsure when I first saw her, but now it's beyond all question – we have found the real Angelica.
